title: Access control verification and SIEM contract for external assessment
content:
Purpose:
This doc is the working contract for an upcoming third-party security assessment that will: verify access-control (RBAC v2) enforcement across management and runtime planes, validate audit log completeness and tamper-evidence, and define the SIEM export schema + automated evidence packaging required for external reviewers and internal verification.

High-level objectives:
- Confirm RBAC v2 role bindings, admin bypass controls, and cross-tenant isolation under test scenarios.
- Validate audit log schema, retention, and integrity guarantees for sensitive events (auth, role change, key management, delegation, model-publish).
- Provide a machine-readable SIEM export contract (fields + types) and demonstrate automated exports into the assessment evidence bundle.
- Produce prioritized remediation plan and verification checklist for sign-off.

Scope (in-scope):
- Management API endpoints that modify roles and permissions (internal console, API tokens).
- VPC/private deployment control-plane actions that affect tenant routing or key material access.
- Audit log pipelines: app logs -> log-collector -> SIEM export (S3/secure endpoint).
- Evidence automation: hashing, signing, and replay snippets to show sequence and timestamps.

Out-of-scope:
- Vendor firmware / hardware-level testing (GPUs or BOM).
- Full application penetration tests unrelated to access control (e.g., prompt-injection tests for deployed models).

Success criteria (must pass to close engagement):
- Reproducible test cases demonstrating RBAC denial + grant semantics across 5 role archetypes (sysadmin, infra-ops, tenant-admin, read-only-audit, service-account).
- Audit log completeness: >=99.9% of test actions present, no gaps >1s in event ordering for assessment window.
- Evidence bundle format: compressed archive with manifest.json, SHA256 hashes, detached signature (ed25519), and SIEM CSV/NDJSON export that matches contract.

Assessment timeline (proposed):
- Week 0: Intake meeting, exchange of scope doc + allowlist, create temporary assessment accounts.
- Week 1: Adversary emulation & RBAC tests (guided).
- Week 2: Audit log ingestion & SIEM export verification, evidence automation validation.
- Week 3: Findings review and draft remediation plan.
- Week 4: Final report delivery and remediation sign-off.

Roles & contacts:
- Internal lead (security): Avery Chen (owner) – overall coordination, evidence packaging, verification.
- Platform SME: Marcus Patel – RBAC v2 implementation, access routes, test harness.
- Logging & SIEM: Elena Soto – export endpoints, index mapping.
- SRE / infra: Priya Nair – temporary infra for assessment, retention, bucket policies.
- Third-party vendor primary: (to be filled by vendor).

Pre-engagement checklist (items to complete before tests begin):
- Create assessment accounts with role matrix attached (CSV).
- Provide allowlist CIDR ranges for vendor IPs.
- Enable verbose audit logging for assessment window.
- Provision a read-only SIEM export endpoint (S3 prefix with kms key) and temporary credentials.
- Create test dataset and seed transactions to exercise role boundaries.

SIEM export contract (fields & types) - canonical mapping (CSV/NDJSON expected):
- timestamp: ISO-8601 string (e.g., 2026-03-01T16:23:45.123Z)
- event_id: UUIDv4 string
- service: string (e.g., auth, iam, model-publish, console)
- action: string (verb, e.g., role.assign, token.create, login.failure)
- actor_type: string (user | service | api-key)
- actor_id: string (email or service id)
- target_type: string (role | project | key | model)
- target_id: string
- outcome: string (success | failure | partial)
- request_id: string (correlation id)
- source_ip: ip-string
- user_agent: string
- request_payload_hash: SHA256 hex
- prev_event_hash: SHA256 hex (for lightweight chaining)
- signature: base64 (optional, populated by collector)
- retention_ttl_days: integer (metadata only)

Minimum payload example (NDJSON line):
{"timestamp":"2026-03-01T16:23:45.123Z","event_id":"d9f8a3b2-...","service":"iam","action":"role.assign","actor_type":"user","actor_id":"marcus@redwood.ai","target_type":"role","target_id":"tenant-admin","outcome":"success","request_id":"r-1234","source_ip":"203.0.113.5","request_payload_hash":"e3b0c442...","prev_event_hash":"","signature":""}

Log integrity & tamper-evidence approach:
- Each log event will include request_payload_hash. The collector will compute archive-level SHA256 over a contiguous window and write manifest entries with archive_hash and timestamp.
- Evidence packaging must include manifest.json with fields: archive_prefix, start_ts, end_ts, archive_sha256, signed_by (internal key id), signature_base64.
- Provide detached signature using team signing key (ed25519) for the manifest. Verification steps are documented in the packaging runbook below.

Evidence packaging runflow (automated):
1) At assessment close window, trigger collector snapshot job (collector-tag: assessment-v1).
2) Collector writes NDJSON to s3://redwood-assessment/<vendor>/<run-timestamp>/events.ndjson
3) Collector computes SHA256 per-line and overall archive sha256 -> writes manifest.json.
4) Signing service signs manifest.json and writes manifest.sig.
5) Packaging tool bundles events.ndjson + manifest.json + manifest.sig + provenance.txt into events-<run>.tar.gz and computes final SHA256.
6) Upload final bundle to s3://redwood-assessment-exports/<vendor>/ and share presigned link to vendor.

Commands (examples):
- compute file hash: sha256sum events.ndjson > events.ndjson.sha256
- sign manifest (ed25519): ed25519-sign --key /keys/sec-team-ed25519.pem manifest.json > manifest.sig
- verify: ed25519-verify --pub /keys/sec-team-ed25519.pub manifest.json manifest.sig

S3 naming and lifecycle contract:
- Export prefix: s3://redwood-assessment-exports/<vendor>/<assessment-id>/run-<ts>/events-<ts>.tar.gz
- KMS: Use assessment-specific KMS key; key rotation policy recorded in manifest.
- ACLs: Block public ACLs; object lock disabled for assessment exports (explicit approval required).

Remediation plan template (deliverable):
- For each finding include: id, title, severity (critical/high/medium/low), scope, reproduction steps, root cause hypothesis, recommended fix, owner, ETA, verification steps, linked tickets.

Prioritization & SLAs (recommended):
- Critical: fix within 72 hours, hotfix rollback plan required, weekly status updates.
- High: fix within 14 days, validate in staging, patch schedule.
- Medium: fix within 30 days, include in next sprint.
- Low: triage for backlog, optional.

Sample (fictional) findings summary - for illustration only:
- FIND-001 (Critical): "Service-account token reuse allowed across tenants" -> Impact: privilege escalation across tenants if SA tokens leaked. Owner: Platform SME. ETA: 72h. Remediation: enforce tenant-scoped tokens, rotate existing tokens, add token binding to tenant id.
- FIND-002 (High): "Audit log missing request_payload_hash for console role changes" -> Impact: reduces tamper-evidence. Remediation: instrument console controller to compute payload hash and surface in log emitter. ETA: 14 days.
- FIND-003 (Medium): "SIEM export mapping for action 'model.publish' missing 'model_id' field in some events" -> Remediation: schema enforcement in collector and unit tests. ETA: 30 days.

Ticket template (example body for Linear/JIRA):
Title: [SEC][FIND-002] Add request_payload_hash to console role-change events
Description: Steps to reproduce, expected log fields (see SIEM contract), observed event payload sample, suggested code changes (logging middleware), test plan, owners.

Communication & escalation plan:
- Immediate: open incident channel #sec-assessment-<id> in Slack for live coordination.
- Daily standups during remediation week (15m).
- Escalation to security director if critical remains open after SLA window.

Verification & acceptance criteria (post-remediation):
- For each closed finding, vendor reproduces steps against patched environment and confirms no regression.
- Internal automation will run a verification harness that replays 100 canonical actions and checks for presence + correct fields in SIEM export.

Appendix: artifacts to hand over to vendor at assessment start:
- Role matrix CSV (format: role,principal,scope,source-ticket)
- Allowlist IPs & short-lived credentials (vault path)
- SIEM export sample file (NDJSON) with 1k synthetic events
- Evidence packaging script (packaging.sh) and signing public key

Notes/known constraints:
- We cannot provide production customer data; assessment will run on sanitized test tenants.
- For Private deployments, additional steps for air-gapped evidence transfer will be used (scp to agreed bastion).

Open questions (to resolve in intake):
- Vendor requested: exact time-window length for log ordering guarantees (default 5 minutes).
- Decide if detached signatures use internal key or third-party escrow key.

Next steps:
- Lock intake date with vendor; confirm vendor PII handling and insurance; create assessment workspace in Linear and Confluence; populate role matrix and sample NDJSON by end of Week 0.

Document version history:
- v0.1 (2025-11-04) initial draft by Avery Chen
- v0.2 (2026-01-12) added packaging runflow and sample fields (Elena Soto)
- v0.3 (2026-03-01) updated timelines and verification harness notes (Marcus Patel)

End of document.
